sentences.text: 1. Aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 05.12.2019 passed in MVC No.98/2018 by the I Additional District and Sessions Judge, D.K., Mangaluru (for short 'the Tribunal'), the petitioners therein have preferred this appeal.

entities.text: I Additional District and Sessions Judge, D.K., Mangaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to herein as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 08.11.2017, at about 9.15 a.m., the deceased Narayan @ Narayana Naik was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-19/EH-267 from Beluvai towards Moodabidre and when he reached Kandige Darkhasu Mugerkal, Beluvai Village, Mangaluru at about 6.10 p.m., the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-19/U-6176, duly insured with respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and being driven in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against the deceased, because of which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died.
Hence, petitioner Nos.1 & 2, who are the parents of the deceased and petitioner Nos.3 Sri Sesappa Naik vs National Insurance Company Ltd on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171546568/
2 and 4, who are the sisters of the deceased filed MVC.No.98/2018.
4.

entities.text: Sri Sesappa Naik vs National Insurance Company Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Based on the pleadings and the evidence let in, the Tribunal concluded that the accident happened due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle, which was duly insured with respondent No.2 - Insurance company and the Tribunal awarded a compensation of Rs.11,82,000/-
to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition, till its realization.
Not satisfied by the same, the petitioners have preferred this appeal.
5. Admittedly, the accident is of the year 2017.
Petitioners have not proved the income of the deceased before the Tribunal.
In the absence of proof of income, as per the chart prepared by the Lok-Adalath, the notional income to be taken for the year 2017 is Rs.11,000/- per month.
The deceased was aged about 33 years at the time of the accident.
As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121], a multiplier of '16' has to be adopted.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in [2009(6) SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the law laid down by the Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% needs to be added to his income asfuture prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since he was a bachelor, 50% has to be deducted.
Petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are his parents.
Petitioner Nos.3 & 4 are his sisters.

Thus, towards loss of dependency, the petitioners would be entitled to a sum of Rs.14,78,400/-(11,000x12x16+40% x 1/2).
6.

Further, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644], there are four dependants and they are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium(Rs.40,000x4=1,60,000).

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
v. Somwati [(2020)9 SCC 644]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, petitioners are also entitled to a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Thus, in all, they are entitled to a sum of Rs.16,68,400/-.

7. Hence, the following:-
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The total compensation awarded by the  Tribunal is modified and enhanced to Rs.16,68,400/- as against Rs.11,82,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of the claim petition till its realization.

iii. The petitioners are entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.4,86,400/- over and above what has been already awarded by the Tribunal along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition before the Tribunal till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

iv. The enhanced compensation amount  shall also be apportioned between the  petitioners in the manner ordered by the Sri Sesappa Naik vs National Insurance Company Ltd on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171546568/
3 Tribunal regarding the compensation awarded by it.
